_comment: Edit wording freely. Fields per ticket: summary (unique), status (todo|in_progress|done), status_note, priority (Highest|High|Medium|Low|Lowest), labels (no spaces; 'ap-automation' is always added), sections [{heading, paragraphs[], bullets[]}], acceptance_criteria[], links[]. Use `backticks` for inline code/paths. Summaries are the idempotency key: changing one makes the script treat it as a new ticket.

sections.heading: Goal
paragraphs: Prove that a self-learning, governed GL-coding system can auto-post a meaningful share of non-PO invoices at a very low false-positive rate, first in shadow mode on a client's own history, before any live posting.
Plan order: client pilot first (data access, discovery, one agreed success number), then the numbered steps below.

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Non-PO invoice GL coding via retrieval, a governed confidence gate and a human-in-the-loop write-back
Evaluation on synthetic data (done), public data (rehearsal) and the client's real history (the number that matters)
Client onboarding: data-readiness check, shadow mode, go/no-go

acceptance_criteria: Headline success number agreed with the client and measured on their data in shadow mode
All child tickets Done or consciously deferred to the Later backlog

tickets.summary: Client pilot: data access, discovery and success metric

sections.heading: Why
paragraphs: Everything downstream depends on the client's real history. This is the first thing to unblock: without data access and an agreed success number, the evaluation numbers cannot be quoted.

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Data-sharing agreement, NDA and DPA in place before any data moves
Confirm the ERP, and the non-PO invoice volume per month
Obtain 12 months of confirmed invoices with fields: vendor, description, amount, currency, entity, cost centre, posted GL code
Decide where it runs: data stays in a client-controlled environment (not the Render free tier)
Agree ONE headline success number up front, e.g. auto-post X% of non-PO invoices at under 1% false positives in shadow mode

acceptance_criteria: Data-sharing agreement, NDA and DPA signed
ERP and monthly non-PO invoice volume confirmed in writing
12 months of confirmed invoices received with all seven required fields
Hosting location agreed: client-controlled environment, data never on the Render free tier
Headline success metric (X% auto-post at under 1% false positives, shadow mode) agreed and recorded

tickets.summary: Embeddings model: fix text-embedding-3-small and record it in evaluations
tickets.status_note: The live evaluation is finished; one small follow-up remains (record the model name in the evaluation JSON).

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: Live OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` run on the synthetic set versus the control:
bullets: Automation 76.6% vs 68.0% control
Auto-post accuracy 99.5% (3 wrong of 613)
21/21 anomalies caught; 187/187 forced auto-posts refused; 0 learned
Repeatable to within one invoice across runs
`text-embedding-3-large` showed no measurable benefit

sections.heading: Decision
paragraphs: Use `text-embedding-3-small`. Fix the model and version before onboarding any client.
Reminder: `EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS` must change with the model (3072 for 3-large); changing the model requires re-embedding the corpus.

acceptance_criteria: Model name and version pinned in configuration before client onboarding
TODO: record the embedding model name in the evaluation JSON output (`scripts/evaluate_poc.py`)
Note in the docs that EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS must match the model (3072 for 3-large)

tickets.summary: Real-data evaluation on the client's history

sections.heading: Scope
paragraphs: Replay about 12 months of the client's history, with write-back, and report honestly.
bullets: Report auto-post accuracy, false-positive rate, automation vs control, and calibration by confidence band
Check the current thresholds on real data: minimum evidence 3, MDM 0.85, agreement 0.80, confidence 0.50
Change thresholds only through the evaluation, never by hand-tuning against a single run

acceptance_criteria: Replay of about 12 months completed with write-back
Auto-post accuracy, false-positive rate, automation vs control and per-band calibration reported
Thresholds (min evidence 3, MDM 0.85, agreement 0.80, confidence 0.50) reviewed; any change justified by the evaluation
Results written to a dated evaluation JSON under docs/

tickets.summary: Public-data replay (rehearsal): City of Los Angeles Checkbook L.A.
tickets.status_note: Another background task is currently building the replay.

sections.heading: Scope
paragraphs: Stand-in and rehearsal for the real-data evaluation. Dataset: City of Los Angeles Checkbook L.A. (Socrata dataset `pggv-e4fn`, CC BY 4.0).
bullets: NEVER use account_name, expenditure_type or item_code_name as features: they leak the label
Run the same replay and reporting as the client evaluation so the pipeline is rehearsed end to end

sections.heading: Limits to state with every number
bullets: Public-sector fund accounting
Mostly PO-linked spend
No VAT and no multi-entity
Labels are posted ledger values, not clerk decisions
Do NOT quote its accuracy as private-sector accuracy

acceptance_criteria: Replay completes using `scripts/replay_public_data.py` with the leakage columns excluded
Results report includes the limits listed above
Accuracy is labelled as a rehearsal number, not a private-sector claim

tickets.summary: Data-readiness check for client onboarding

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Score a client's history on coding consistency, vendor coverage and chart-of-accounts match
Define a minimum score to go live
Clients below the minimum start in suggest-only mode
Learn the real bar from the first clients; do not over-fit the threshold up front

acceptance_criteria: Readiness score implemented with the three components and reported per client
Minimum go-live score defined and documented (provisional)
Failing clients are automatically placed in suggest-only mode
Process to revisit the bar after the first clients is written down

tickets.summary: Ambiguity report: reduce ambiguous invoices over time

sections.heading: Why
paragraphs: In the Checkbook L.A. replay 89% of vendors used more than one account code and nearly all review reasons were 'evidence disagrees'. More data alone did not remove that ambiguity (automation rose from about 63% to 67% and then levelled off), because the ambiguity comes from how the organisation codes invoices. Reducing it needs decisions from the client's team, not just learning.

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Ambiguity report for a client: list vendors and description patterns where past coding is split, with the accounts used and how often, ranked by invoice volume
Let the client's team confirm the preferred rule for each ambiguous pattern (for example 'cleaning goes to 6300 unless it is for the warehouse'); record the decision, who made it and when
Feed confirmed rules back so those cases become automatable, and keep them auditable and versioned
Track 'share of invoices in ambiguous vendors' month by month as a metric
Flag near-duplicate accounts in the chart of accounts that clerks use interchangeably
Keep clerk effort light: one short confirmation per ambiguous pattern, ranked by volume

sections.heading: Notes
paragraphs: Frame it to the client as improving the consistency of their own coding with their team, not as replacing clerks; clerk cooperation is what supplies the corrections the system learns from.

acceptance_criteria: Report generated from a client's history (public LA data used as the rehearsal), showing split-coded vendors and patterns ranked by volume
Confirmed rules are stored with author and timestamp, and applied by the gate in a versioned, replayable way
Ambiguous-vendor share is reported per month and shown trending in the shadow-mode report
Measured effect: automation and auto-post accuracy before and after confirming the top N ambiguous patterns

tickets.summary: Test the untested paths: live Claude LLM gate and specialist-agent ablation

sections.heading: Live Claude LLM gate
bullets: Escalation-only: it may only ever tighten a decision, never loosen it
Measure the escalation rate
Define and test behaviour when the LLM is unavailable (fail safe)

sections.heading: Ablation of specialist agents
paragraphs: Ablate the entity, VAT and cost-centre agents one at a time. Measure errors prevented vs correct auto-posts blocked. `vat_review_required` is the largest review reason, so start there.

acceptance_criteria: Live Claude gate run on the evaluation set; escalation rate reported
Test proves the gate can only tighten (never turn a refusal into an auto-post)
Behaviour when the LLM is unavailable is tested and documented
Ablation report for entity, VAT and cost-centre agents: errors prevented vs correct auto-posts blocked

tickets.summary: Shadow mode with a client: 30 days predicting without posting

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Run for 30 days predicting GL codes without posting anything
Go/no-go: false-positive rate under 1% of would-be auto-posts
Clients below the readiness score start in suggest-only mode

acceptance_criteria: 30 days of shadow predictions captured against actual clerk postings
False-positive rate computed as a share of would-be auto-posts; go/no-go recorded (under 1% to go)
Readiness-score gate applied: below-threshold clients stay suggest-only
Results reviewed with the client against the agreed headline success number

tickets.summary: Housekeeping: rotate secrets, fix CI token scope, check env vars and deck numbers

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Rotate the GitHub tokens (currently embedded in git remote URLs) and the Render key
Issue a token with the `workflow` scope so CI files (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) can be pushed
Confirm Vercel and Render environment variables: AP_API_URL and AP_API_KEY
Check whether the business-case deck or client packs reuse old fabricated UI numbers

acceptance_criteria: GitHub tokens rotated and git remote URLs no longer contain credentials
Render key rotated and redeployed
New GitHub token with `workflow` scope can push CI files
AP_API_URL and AP_API_KEY verified on Vercel and Render
Business-case deck and client packs checked; any old fabricated UI numbers replaced with evaluation-backed numbers

tickets.summary: Gate and retrieval tuning on the public replay (LA Checkbook)

sections.heading: Why
paragraphs: First real-data replay: automation 65.1% (control 53.2%), auto-post accuracy 87.0%, GL accuracy 74.0%, vendor-most-common baseline 70.0%. The gate is too loose for vendors with mixed coding; retrieval ignores department, fund and amount; accuracy decays from about 91% to 80% over the year.

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Department, fund and amount band as extra evidence signals (config flag, off by default)
Stricter gate: agreement, minimum evidence, top-account margin, diversity-scaled evidence
Recency weighting against drift
Coverage-versus-accuracy curve; coverage reachable at 95%, 98% and 99% auto-post accuracy
Tune on early months, report on held-out later months, with confidence intervals

acceptance_criteria: Variants compared on a held-out window with Wilson confidence intervals
Coverage at 95/98/99% auto-post accuracy reported, or shown unreachable
Default production behaviour and docs/evaluation.json numbers unchanged
Findings that generalise vs LA-specific effects stated explicitly

tickets.summary: Calibrated confidence score

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Replace the hand-weighted 0.7/0.3 mix with a score fitted to observed outcomes (for example logistic regression on agreement, similarity, evidence count, vendor code diversity)
Fit per client on their own confirmed history; keep a simple fallback
Report calibration by band and expected calibration error before and after

acceptance_criteria: Calibration error reported on a held-out window and improved against the current score
Fitted parameters versioned and recorded with each prediction
A stated confidence band (for example 0.95+) maps to a measured accuracy

tickets.summary: Per-vendor thresholds and drift detection

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Per-vendor adaptive thresholds: stricter for vendors with many distinct account codes, looser for single-code vendors with long history
Detect per-vendor drift (recent coding differs from long-run coding) and lower confidence or send to review
Monthly per-vendor accuracy monitoring in the performance view

acceptance_criteria: Measured effect on auto-post accuracy and coverage on the replay (held-out window)
Drift alerts raised in a replay where the coding of a vendor changes mid-year
Thresholds auditable and versioned

tickets.summary: Clerk measurement for shadow mode (override reasons, agreement, sampled review)

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Capture a short reason whenever a clerk overrides a suggestion (wrong department, policy changed, wrong account, other)
Record clerk identity and timestamp; measure agreement between clerks on the same vendor
Sampled blind review of would-be auto-posts to measure an honest false-positive rate
Measure time per invoice with and without suggestions
Keep clerk effort light: no extra clicks to confirm a correct suggestion
Only human-confirmed lines go into the corpus

acceptance_criteria: Override reasons stored and reported by category
Clerk-agreement measure reported per vendor
Random sample of would-be auto-posts reviewed each week with a reported error rate
Time-per-invoice comparison available for the manager report

tickets.summary: Evidence panel and two-candidate suggestions in the review UI

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Show similar past invoices behind each suggestion: description, account, who coded it, when, and similarity
When two accounts are close, show both candidates with their evidence so the clerk can pick quickly
Show any agent flag and the reason an invoice went to review

acceptance_criteria: Every suggestion lists its evidence with account, coder and date
Close calls show two candidates with a measured share of the vote
Clerks can accept or choose in one action

tickets.summary: Weekly manager report for shadow mode

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: One page per week: invoices processed, share the system could have auto-posted, accuracy, false positives from the sampled review, time saved, ambiguity trend
Plain language for finance directors; numbers labelled as shadow-mode measurements
Export to PDF or a shareable page

acceptance_criteria: Report generated automatically from shadow-mode data
All figures traceable to the audit log
Reviewed with the client's finance lead before the first pilot

tickets.summary: Deterministic deployment profile for sceptical clients

sections.heading: Why
paragraphs: One client wants everything deterministic and no AI at runtime, and distrusts RAG solutions. The decision path is already rule-based and the LLM gate can only escalate; this makes it explicit and verifiable.

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Profile with a pinned embedding model or a local open model (no external calls at runtime)
LLM gate off by default; it can only ever send an invoice to review
Nightly batch learning with a versioned corpus snapshot; any prediction can be replayed exactly
Record model, configuration and corpus version with every prediction
Describe the system to this client as a transparent lookup of how their team coded similar invoices, with the evidence shown

acceptance_criteria: Replaying a stored prediction against its recorded corpus version gives the same result
No outbound AI calls in the deterministic profile (verified by test)
Provenance fields present in the audit record

tickets.summary: Accountant review of methodology and a sample of results

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: After the first client data run, prepare an anonymised sample of about 100 lines (prediction, evidence, outcome, mix of right, wrong and reviewed) for blind review
Review the definition of 'correct', the VAT, entity and cost-centre logic, and the business case assumptions
Prefer an independent or client-side accountant; obtain a short written sign-off with caveats

acceptance_criteria: Sample file produced from real client results
Accountant's verdicts compared with system outcomes
Written sign-off or list of corrections received

tickets.summary: Business case and pitch: capacity framing and honest claims

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Frame the value as capacity, speed and auditability; do not promise removing clerks
Use shadow-mode measurements to price the saving per client
Show synthetic and public-data results side by side, labelled, including weaknesses
Check any deck or pack for the old fabricated UI numbers

acceptance_criteria: Pitch and business case contain no unmeasured accuracy claims
Cost-per-invoice and time-saved assumptions documented and reviewed
Old fabricated figures removed from all client-facing material

tickets.summary: Record the LA replay result in README and v2 docs

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Add the public-data replay results next to the synthetic ones in the README and the v2 documents
State what the public data does and does not show (public-sector fund accounting, labels fixed at PO stage, no VAT)
Keep the synthetic 99.8% labelled as synthetic everywhere it appears

acceptance_criteria: README and affected v2 documents updated and consistent with docs/public_replay_*.json
No document presents synthetic accuracy as real-world accuracy

tickets.summary: Code hygiene: fix existing lint errors and commit the current work

sections.heading: Scope
bullets: Fix the roughly 30 existing ruff errors outside the governed paths
Commit and push the uncommitted work in sensible groups (docs, Jira tooling, replay scripts, evaluation outputs)
Keep data/public/ and jira_created.json out of git

acceptance_criteria: ruff clean across the repository
All current work committed and pushed
